problems.label: Binge-compensation cycle
definitions: Has episodes of eating a large amount with a sense of losing control, several times a month or more.
Tries to undo eating by vomiting, laxatives, fasting or hard exercise.
Feels that self-worth depends on shape and weight, and hides eating from others.
longTermGoals: Binges and compensation stop or become rare, eating is regular, and self-worth rests on more than shape and weight.

shortTermObjectives.text: Within 1 week, attend a medical assessment, and agree with the care team which warning signs (fainting, chest pain, very low weight) mean same-day care.
Within 4 weeks, start eating-disorder-focused guided self-help or CBT and complete weekly self-monitoring.
By week 4, eat 3 meals and 2 or 3 snacks a day at planned times on at least 5 days a week.
Use a distress tolerance skill during at least 3 binge or purge urges a week and record the outcome.
Practice a kind self-statement after any binge, instead of compensating, for 4 weeks.
If binge frequency has not dropped by week 8, discuss a medication evaluation as an adjunct.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit.
